# 2026-11-04 — Follow-up 18

## Diagnosis before changes

At baseline `6f52dfc9491db5c6893c681e88742f43b2251117`, the stale-deadline
reading is supported. Run `b2de46c8-7611-4b7c-8863-2345ff2b0240` does **not**
show forwarding beyond the node's accepted deadline. Its failed row remains
failed. Two details cannot be stated as the prompt suggests: the two held
checks were retries of one Docker invocation, and the retained records omit
the renewed lease's ID and signed issue time. Those omissions are explicit
below; neither is evidence of a product deadline breach. PR #460's body and
Follow-up 17's report were read and compared with the actual records.

### Held checks and all waits

`tests/e2e/at/secops/followup11_transports_test.go:151–180` first polls central
`serving_leases` for up to 90s (one-second sleeps), stores the latest issued
row, then calls `timeoutView` followed by `heartbeatView`. The lease-expiry
case's first Docker invocation after the successful read is therefore
`docker exec fvpn-w4-secops-node nft -j list set inet fvpn allowed_v4`
(`deadline_live_test.go:289–299`). `live_test.go:366–367` passes it through PATH
with only the test context. The nested wrapper generated under `.agent/tmp`
by `admitted.py:21–39` checks `$FVPN_HOLD_SH`, logs one line, sleeps **60s**,
and retries that **same command**, up to ten checks (nine sleeps, 540s).
It does not return to Go between checks.

[Admission receipts](history/follow-up-17/followup17-admission.json) contain
held answers at 06:34:21Z and 06:35:21Z, then free at 06:36:21Z and another
free at 06:36:22Z. The separate private admission log lines 2305–2308 agree.
Both held checks therefore precede the timeout-set read; the following
`docker exec ... cat /run/vpn-node/heartbeat` is a separate free check.
This command attribution follows sequential control flow, not recorded argv:
the historical receipt records only command basename. It would be inaccurate
to claim two different Docker commands each independently waited once.

From the deadline read through the last cutoff sample, all potential waits are:

- The remainder of the 90s central query loop, including SQL calls bounded only
  by the test context and one-second retries. Its final successful row supplies
  the old D; no later lease read exists in this case.
- Both view commands above, worker `docker pause`, control `docker stop --time
  2`, each status/counter Docker read, `PauseAgent`'s Docker touch, and the
  agent SIGKILL Docker exec. Each could invoke the wrapper's 540s admission
  loop; otherwise most use only the test context, whose enclosing Go timeout
  is **45m** (`followup11_run.py:61`). The stop grace is 2s, not a 2s command
  timeout. No fault-command retry exists in Go.
- Two status/counter reads surrounding the unchanged **3s** diagnostic
  (`followup11_transports_test.go:210–219`), then samples with **1s** sleeps
  until D+3s (227–230), followed by two cutoff samples separated by **10s**
  (231–235). `sampleTransport11:19–22` reads status and counters sequentially.
- Status and counter commands have no shorter outer timeout
  (`tests/e2e/established.go:38–65,181–202`). Counter parse-failure evidence
  export can run further Docker reads with a **5s** context (62 onward).
  These are diagnostic reads, not a transport retry.

Recovery readiness (40s), flow retries (120s, 2s sleeps), restart/unpause,
post-cutoff views and fleet restoration follow the last cutoff sample; they
are outside the requested section. No predicate or timeout is changed here.

### The enforced deadline and what the records prove

`node/agent/sync.go:300–344` verifies and accepts the signed lease, stores its
request CLOCK_MONOTONIC anchor and envelope in local SQLite. Same-ID replay
retains the original anchor. `decide.go:620–700` intersects node lease duration,
member/grant and binding limits with that anchor and hands `DeadlineMono` to
enforcement. `node/enforce/deadline.go:36–60`, `apply.go:180–217` and
`render_nft.go:98,138–140,189–191` install bounded timeout elements in
`inet fvpn allowed_v4`; source/destination membership drops precede forwarding.
Those kernel elements expire even with control down and the agent killed.
The temporary `fv_deadline_guard` chain protects installation and is removed
after success; it is not a timer that must be driven by the killed agent.
The independent watchdog can also withdraw the baseline.

Read-only views are the accepted local lease/anchor (`leaseprobe/main.go:24–49`),
heartbeat `policy_expires_mono_ns` (`engine.go:1535–1539`,
`deadlines.go:32–53`: last installed binding deadline), and nft JSON timeout /
expires for `allowed_v4`. The heartbeat need not equal an individual earlier
grant end; the case must take the earlier grant end where appropriate.

[Failure receipt](history/follow-up-17/followup17-lease-expiry-finding.json)
`details.recorded_lease` names generation **14**, issued
**06:34:21.397505Z**, expired **06:35:21.397505Z**. It contains neither lease ID
nor anchor nor signed cap. Fault start is **06:36:22.059987198Z**, 60.662482s
past that cached expiry. [Live record](history/follow-up-17/followup17-transports-live.json)
`transport_cases.lease_expiry.before_heartbeat` and `after_heartbeat` both
show generation14 and **D=97658778490379 ns**, heartbeat wall
1793774181418229445 / mono97623869605414. Its kernel timeout view has 34s
remaining before the fault and 19s after the cutoff samples. The restart
actually adopts the same installed generation14/D at **06:36:37.101Z**
([diagnostic](history/follow-up-17/followup17-diagnostic.json),
`agent_restart_excerpts`, source `lease_expiry-after-agent.log:2`).

The wall/monotonic pair maps D to approximately **06:36:56.327115Z**, not the
cached 06:35:21.397505Z. A 60s lease's request anchor would be approximately
**06:35:56.327115Z**. This is an **inference about request time**, not a signed
issue timestamp. The generation14 renewal is demonstrated by the later
installed deadline, positive kernel remaining lifetime and restart adoption;
its exact lease ID and signed issue time were **not retained**. The case never
read its local lease; the next local read belongs to the subsequent live-agent
case, lease `bef669a3`, generation16, issued06:36:52.273355057Z, and cannot be
substituted. Cleanup removed the old store. Exact historical renewal identity
cannot honestly be reconstructed from these records.

Cutoff observations at **06:36:26.006219887Z** and **06:36:36.221762235Z**
ended 30.325212390s and 20.117164530s before the held heartbeat D; both TCP
and UDP counts increased **322→342**. The sampling loop to cached D+3s was
already over. The quiet predicate correctly failed a wrongly timed window.

## Harness change and offline proof

`timing_admission.py` owns D-160's journal and marker protocol. Each Go case
calls `beginTimed18` before its first deadline read (or relay clock), waits for
free there, then records the start. The private generated wrappers consult
that marker, recording command execution without asking admission. The case
records its end after its last cutoff sample, including early-return closure.
Checks outside sections retain their UTC/monotonic start, completion and
free/held answer without private reasons or foreign arguments. The committed
offline validator rejects missing boundaries, missing free boundary admission,
any check overlapping a section, or a mismatch between Go rows and the journal.
D-133 monitoring is independent and never delays a timed section.

The old case retains the central read and now also records its accepted local
lease before the fault. After `docker stop` returns it reads local SQLite and
the heartbeat again. `faultDeadline18` requires a successful local read,
identity/anchor, signed cap60, duration(0,60s], exact heartbeat D and a future
D at read completion. An earlier grant end wins. The loop uses a Go monotonic
clock deadline mapped from that accepted CLOCK_MONOTONIC D. Rejection names
ID, generation, issue time, cap, duration, lease D, heartbeat D and local-read
status. Stop/kill/read times and both leases are retained. The original cap
is read and restoration registered before its mutation; process restoration
closes the section first. No product or SQL mutation is introduced.

The three-second diagnostic, D+3s loop, ten-second quiet test, recovery and
attribution limit are unchanged. All other case predicates are unchanged;
Follow-up16's evaluator/synthetic tests and Follow-up17's qualification/tests
are byte-identical to baseline. Their offline proofs pass, including H-1
early withdrawal and replies beyond D+3s. New proofs select a renewed lease's
D, reject expired/over-cap/nonlocal/mismatching rereads and reject the historical generation14 record with heartbeat
D97658778490379. Missing fields in that historical record remain missing;
zero-valued decoded fields do not assert an actual signed cap0.

The Python admission proof exercises held→free, proving the section waits
60s before starting; no check is made for a nested command during the section.
Injected held **and free** checks inside a section both invalidate evidence.
A synthetic clock fixture initially reused a timestamp and failed this strict
audit; the fixture was corrected. Initial e2e-only staticcheck found an
integration-only helper in the e2e file; it was moved to the integration file.
Both initial failures and final verification are retained in this run's records.

## Pre-subject wrapper stop and authorized rerun

The first dispatch on `b3c5d680` passed preflight at07:43Z but never reached
`make`, stack setup or a Go sub-case. The new admission implementation inherited
the wrapped PATH; `$FVPN_HOLD_SH` invokes Python, which recursively entered the
wrapper. The foreground owner's tree was stopped and killed (11,215 owned
processes); no foreign process was signalled. Independent inventory found zero
owned containers/images/networks/volumes and zero active timing-helper processes.
This is a harness defect, not a sub-case result. The invocation now uses the
original unwrapped PATH, as the previous wrapper did. A regression test runs a
hold script that itself invokes Python while a failing fake Python wrapper is
first on PATH. It passes only with the original PATH restored. All45 Python
tests and Go area tests pass; an actual nested-admission smoke check also passed.

The original preflight, overlap journal and two admission receipts are retained
at `history/follow-up-18-pre-subject/`, with stop/inventory receipts and SHA-256
pins. The sole allowed pre-subject harness rerun is used after this fix is
committed. There is no authorization for any further rerun or failed sub-case
retry. The recorded 180s initial admission wait remains part of the120-minute
budget. The recursion is routed as a harness incident with its receipts.
